title: Word counter
brief: Print the number of lines, words and characters in the input, like the Unix wc command, separated by spaces. A word is a run of characters that are not spaces, tabs or newlines. Every character counts, including newlines.
stdin:
hello world
this is a test
hints: Three rules are enough: one for a word, one for a newline, and one for anything else.
yyleng holds the length of the current match, so a word adds yyleng to the character count.
A word pattern can be written as [^ \t\n]+, which means one or more characters that are not whitespace.
explanation: Longest match does the work here: [^ \t\n]+ takes a whole word in one go, so each word fires its rule exactly once. Newlines and other whitespace fall through to the other two rules, which only update the counts.
